title: A relatively ample line module on the stable-curve multidegree-zero Picard space
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $f:C\to S$ be a stable unpointed genus-$g$ family, $g\geq2$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Suppose the subfunctor $D\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{C/S}$ [sk-def-picard-pic] of classes with degree zero on every component of every geometric fibre is represented by an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Here component degree is the degree after pulling the invertible module to the smooth normalization of the component [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], as in the stable-family convention. There is an invertible $\mathcal O_D$-module $\mathcal M$, trivialized along the identity section, which is relatively ample over $S$. Consequently $D$ is a scheme, quasi-projective over $S$. An invertible module on $D$ is a line module on its small etale site [def-trf-algebraic-space]; on a scheme it is the ordinary invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Relative ampleness [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] means that over every affine open of $S$, positive tensor powers of the module have sections giving an affine-open basis on $D$.

source.place: Sections 4.1--4.3, printed pp.141--142, especially Proposition 4.3; the relatively ample line module on the multidegree-zero relative Picard space and scheme representability. Local PDF WANTED; primary Numdam PDF read online.

proof.text: Choose the arithmetic universal presentation $U_\bullet$ and its stable families using [lem-sfb-stable-moduli-regular-universal-atlas]. Their projective-bundle morphisms are proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper]; they are flat and finitely presented with nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric fibres by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. Thus [lem-sc-proper-flat-global-sections] gives universal $f_*\mathcal O=\mathcal O$, and [lem-sfb-picard-space-curves-smooth] represents their full Picard sheaves by group algebraic spaces. The open multidegree-zero subgroup is represented by [lem-sfb-nodal-multidegree-zero-locus]. Denote it $D_n$ on $U_n$. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-picard-etale-schematic]: each $D_n$ is smooth separated of finite presentation, with geometrically integral fibres. Its base-change and curve-isomorphism clauses identify the $D_n$ along the universal nerve. All $U_n$ are regular Noetherian and their smooth-family opens are dense. On those opens $D_n$ is the degree-zero relative Jacobian by the Picard-subfunctor definition.

source.place: Sections 3.2 and 4.2--4.3: universal regular presentation and its Picard spaces.

proof.text: On $D_0|_{U_0^{\mathrm{sm}}}$ take the canonical normalized line $B$ of [lem-sfb-smooth-jacobian-canonical-line]. Extend it to an identity-rigidified line $M_0$ on $D_0$ using [lem-sfb-regular-group-rigidified-line-extension]. Its hypotheses hold by Step 1: $U_0$ is regular Noetherian, $U_0^{\mathrm{sm}}$ is dense, and $D_0$ is smooth separated with geometrically integral fibres. This constructs a line on the entire universal Picard space without choosing a theta divisor on any individual singular fibre.

source.place: Section 4.2, extension and normalization at the identity.

proof.text: Over $U_1$, the two pullbacks of $M_0$ restrict to canonically isomorphic rigidified lines on the smooth-family open, by [lem-sfb-smooth-jacobian-canonical-line]. The uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-regular-group-rigidified-line-extension], applied to $D_1/U_1$, extends that isomorphism uniquely. The projections to $U_0$ are etale; hence the pulled-back extensions are extensions of precisely these restricted lines. On $U_2$, the two composites of overlap isomorphisms restrict to the same canonical isomorphism on the dense smooth open. Uniqueness there makes the composites equal. The same argument gives the identity on the diagonal. Thus $M_0$ has a rigidification-preserving descent cocycle for the universal moduli presentation.

source.place: Section 4.2, uniqueness on overlaps and Cartesian system on the moduli groupoid.

proof.text: For the given $C/S$, let $T=S\times_{\mathfrak M}U_0$ as in [lem-sfb-stable-moduli-regular-universal-atlas]. The universal curve isomorphism and the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-nodal-picard-etale-schematic] identify $D_T$ with the pullback of $D_0$. Pull back $M_0$ to $D_T$ and the cocycle of Step 3 to $T\times_ST$. Refine $T$ by the etale scheme covering in the nodal Picard lemma, so that the resulting $D_{T_a}$ are schemes. Now $D_{T_a}\to D$ is a jointly surjective etale scheme family. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent] to these lines and their cocycle. It produces a line module $M$ on $D$. The local identity trivializations agree because every transition preserves them, and therefore give $e^*M\simeq\mathcal O_S$. This descent uses the universal cocycle, with no regularity assumption on $S$.

source.place: Section 4.2, passage from the universal Cartesian system to arbitrary families.

proof.text: It remains to prove ampleness on the universal base. Choose an etale covering $W_a\to U_0$ on which $D_0\times_{U_0}W_a$ is a scheme, using [lem-sfb-nodal-picard-etale-schematic]. Refine to affine $W_a$. They are regular Noetherian, and the inverse image of $U_0^{\mathrm{sm}}$ is dense. Thus every generic point of $W_a$ lies in that smooth-family open. Over the inverse image of $U_0^{\mathrm{sm}}$, $M_0$ is the pullback of the relatively ample canonical Jacobian line $B$ of Step 2. For a generic point $\eta$ of $W_a$ choose an affine open $W'\subseteq U_0^{\mathrm{sm}}$ containing its image; $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)\to W'$ is a map of affine schemes, so its base change $D_\eta\to D_0\times_{U_0}W'$ is affine. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] makes $M_0|_{D_\eta}$ ample. The group-scheme criterion [lem-sfb-regular-group-generic-ampleness] applies: the groups are smooth separated of finite presentation, and their geometrically integral fibres are connected. It makes $M_0|_{D_{W_a}}$ relatively ample. No ampleness criterion for an algebraic space has been assumed here.

source.place: Sections 4.3 and 4.8, scheme-local reduction before applying Raynaud XI 1.13.

proof.text: Over each affine open of $U_0$, refine the cover in Step 5 to a finite covering by affine etale schemes; it is fpqc. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-ampleness-fpqc-descent] to conclude that $D_0$ is a scheme and $M_0$ is relatively ample. For its pullback along any scheme map $h:B\to U_0$, choose affine opens $W\subseteq U_0$ and $V\subseteq h^{-1}(W)$ covering $B$. The map $V\to W$ is affine: both are affine, and inverse images of standard affine opens are spectra of localizations. Its base change $D_0\times_{U_0}V\to D_0\times_{U_0}W$ is affine, by the tensor-product description of affine base change. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] makes the pulled-back line ample on $D_V$. This proves relative ampleness of the pullback, since it is Zariski local on the base, also a special case of [lem-sfb-space-relative-ampleness-fpqc-descent]. In particular it applies to $T\to U_0$ of Step 4. Over every affine open of $S$, refine the surjective etale $T\to S$ to a finite covering by affine schemes. Apply that same descent theorem to the line $M$ of Step 4 and this fpqc covering. It follows that $D$ is a scheme and $M$ is relatively ample over $S$.

source.place: Section 4.8, base-change stability and etale-local descent of relative ampleness.

proof.text: Finally [lem-sfb-nodal-picard-etale-schematic] gives finite presentation of $D\to S$, so its restriction over any affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is of finite type and quasi-compact. The ample-line immersion theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base] applied to $M|_{D_W}$ supplies $d>0$, an immersion $D_W\to\mathbf P^N_W$, and $M^{\otimes d}\simeq i^*\mathcal O(1)$. This is quasi-projectivity over $S$ (locally on its base) and proves the consequence. All constructions and conclusions restrict to the empty base as well.

source.place: Proposition 4.3, quasi-projectivity consequence; Stacks Tags 01VS and 01VT.

proof_origin.place: Sections 4.1--4.8, pp.141--144, read online at https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1985__127__131_0.pdf; local PDF WANTED. Explicit universal descent assembly follows the source; Raynaud input remains separately stated.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q120-db93d6d10 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The delivery follows Deligne, Le lemme de Gabber, Astérisque 127, which I read from the Numdam scan: §2 p.135-136 (multidegree-zero Pic is separated, smooth, finite type, semi-abelian); 4.1 (smooth Jacobian line (Id,e)^*Poincaré); 4.2 (extension over the regular universal base by the determinant of a coherent extension, rigidification correction, uniqueness from irreducible geometric fibres); 4.3/4.8 (étale-local reduction, then Raynaud LNM 119 XI 1.13; the [8] in 4.8 is a typo for [10]); 4.4-4.6 (étale-local schematicness). I also read Stacks moduli-curves.tex 0E9C (theorem-stable-smooth-proper) and lemma-smooth-dense-in-stable. Raynaud is not available locally and stays WANTED. The generic-ampleness node is consistent with Raynaud VI 2.5 and VIII Thm 2 as quoted in arXiv 2209.02443, and with Deligne's own use of XI 1.13 over a regular base; I accept it as an unsplit input. The item statement differs from the base only by added definition citations. Steps 1-4, 6 and 7 are correct: all hypotheses are checked, the overlap cocycle comes from the uniqueness clause, descent goes through the nodal étale refinement and lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent, fpqc covers are finite affine refinements, affine pullback is justified, and finite presentation gives quasi-projectivity. FIX (C1, step 5): ampleness of M_0 on the generic fibre D_eta needs lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible. The step now argues that Spec kappa(eta) -> W' is affine for an affine W' in U_0^sm, so its base change is affine, and cites the lemma; proof_deps are unchanged. All five new nodes are statement-only and self-contained, with stmt_deps equal to their citations, no SGA, and no duplicates (I compared them with nodal-multidegree-zero-locus, unpointed-stable-coarse-projective, stable-isom-finite-unramified, nodal-curve-stack-smooth, theta-poincare-pullback, abelian-polarization-calculus and normal-base-torsion-frame-extension). The closure is acyclic. I tested the rigidified-extension node by computing the vertical divisor p^*(sum n_i Z_i) and restricting it to e, and checked the nodal node's separatedness via Zariski's lemma. Batch 5: every flagged citation is a definition (def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism, def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres, def-trf-algebraic-space, sk-def-picard-pic, def-sfb-stable-*) or a generic tool (trf ringed-site model, projective-bundle properness, invertible descent, proper-flat global sections, Picard representability of curves). None is a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so all are upheld. The five tool_uses are accepted.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
